newsitem.title: UK: Mark seen propped short-term, awaits Buba meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mark seen propped short-term, awaits Buba meeting.

text.p: The German mark should remain propped by rate speculation early next week, but the unit will stumble if the Bundesbank fails to implement tangible measures and relies only on verbal missives to bolster it, analysts said on Friday.

The fate of the mark -- which jumped against the Euro-crosses, the yen and the dollar this week on expectations German rates were headed higher -- will be determined by the Bundesbank's regular repurchase tender on Tuesday and its first policy meeting after its summer break on Thursday.
"If the Germans don't do anything on Thursday, then the deutschmark could weaken quite significantly," said Mark Geddes, Treasury economist at ABN AMRO.
"Verbally the Bundesbank has done quite well in talking dollar/mark down, but eventually verbal intervention has to be backed up by policy action to work," said Geddes.

Crucial data next week, such as German research institute Ifo's July economic survey on Wednesday and July M3 money supply, will also give the mark direction and clues to future German monetary policy.

These economic indicators, said analysts, are probably going to be relatively supportive of a pick-up in the economy, but analysts said more evidence of an increase in domestic demand is needed before the Bundesbank acts with higher interest rates.
"The Ifo business climate should be improving due to the appreciation of the dollar in July. That might just help improve sentiment," said Ian Morris, international economist at HSBC James Capel.
Against the dollar, the mark gained around five pfennigs from its mid-week lows around 1.87 to test levels below 1.82 marks in afternoon European trade on Friday.

During the week, it also posted hefty gains against its Euro-crosses, pressing to two-month highs of 84.62 against the Spanish peseta and four week highs of 4.1610 and 4.3730, respectively, against the Norwegian and Swedish crowns.
"After this week's gains, there is no doubt the mark will now weaken," said a trader at a UK bank.
But despite a raft of hawkish comments by Bundesbank officials this week, many analysts still say a rate-hike is unlikely at the Bundesbank's policy-making meeting.
"Purely because of the dollar appreciation we think there will be a 20-30 basis point increase in the fixed repo rate. But not next week," said Morris.
Interest rate speculation on currency markets intensified this week after the Bundesbank set this week's repo at an unchanged fixed 3.0 percent without announcing terms for next week's tender.
Credit tightening expectations have also gained momentum after dollar/mark shot to a near-eight year high just over 1.89 marks last week.

The mark began its rally late last week after Bundesbank Chief economist Otmar Issing was quoted as saying that German price developments were moving in the wrong direction and the Bundesbank would carry out its monetary policy according to the national situation.
On Thursday this week, Bundesbank Vice-President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said the German central bank was concerned about signs of continued consumer price inflation adding fuel to the firmer mark.
Although their comments have bolstered the mark, speculation of an imminent rate hike has come off the boil, said analysts.
"I think this mark correction seems to have bought the Buba some time," said ABN's Geddes.
